questions.question: Under what condition is Newton’s second law applicable?
questions.solution_html:
• A particle of mass 2 kg initially at rest, is subjected to a force F= 2e2t Determine v(t)
  • at t = 2s.
  • Mass=2 kg
  • Force F(t)=2e2tN
  • Initial velocity, v(0)=0 Using Newton's second law
  • F= ma, a =F/m
  • a = (2 x 2e2t)/2 = e2t m/s2
  • dv/dt = e2t , solving we get v(2s) = 26.8 m/s (Formula(1 mark), correct answer with units (1mark))

questions.question: Apply the concept of fictitious force to explain why passengers feel pushed outward in a turning car.
questions.solution_html:
• Passengers feel pushed outward because of inertia. When the car turns, a fictitious force called
  • centrifugal force acts outwards. This causes the car to turn, but your body tends to continue the straight
  • line motion due to inertia. This leads to your body being pushed sideways.

questions.question: Why does the day length on Earth slowly increase over millions of years?
questions.solution_html:

  • redistribution of mass and a momentum shift. This slows down the spin of the planet. (page 182; Patrik
  • Hamill)

questions.question: How does Kepler’s third law show that planets farther from the Sun take longer to revolve around it.?
questions.solution_html:
• Kepler’s third law states that the period of a planet squared is proportional to its semimajor axis cubed.
  • Thus, farther planets have greater semimajor axes and longer time periods.
